commands.name: look
commands.summary: Examine your surroundings, look at players, items, containers, or peer in a direction
details_html: The ancient texts speak of observation as the first step toward understanding.
Use this command to examine your surroundings, inspect items, examine containers,
• look [direction] - Look in a specific direction (north, south, east, west, up, down)
• look item [name] - Examine an item (in room, inventory, or equipped)
• look in [container] - Look inside a container to see its contents
• look [name]-[number] or look [name] [number] - Target specific instance when multiple exist
When using ambiguous targets, the system resolves in this order:
When multiple items or containers match a name, use instance numbers:
• look backpack-2 - Look at the second backpack
• look lantern 1 - Look at the first lantern
To see the contents of a container, use the "in" keyword:
• look in backpack - See what's inside your backpack
• look container chest - Examine a chest (shows capacity and lock status)
As the Necronomicon suggests: "That which can be seen may yet remain unseen to the untrained eye."

commands.name: put
commands.summary: Put an item from your inventory into a container
details_html: Transfer items from your inventory into a container. "in" or "into" marks where the item name
ends and the container name begins.
• Items with names of more than one word need "in" or "into": "put folk tonic into chest"
• Without "in"/"into" the first word is the item and the rest is the container
• You can use item names or inventory numbers
• You can specify quantity to put only part of a stack
• Container must be accessible (in room or equipped)
As noted in the restricted archives: "Proper storage of artifacts prevents dimensional contamination."

commands.name: get
commands.summary: Get an item from a container into your inventory
details_html: Transfer items from a container, or from the floor, into your inventory. "from" marks where the
item name ends and the container name begins.
<li>"from" is required to take from a container: "get lantern backpack" looks for an item called
• Item and container names may each be several words
• You can use item names or container item numbers
• You can specify quantity to get only part of a stack
• Container must be accessible (in room or equipped)
As noted in the restricted archives: "Retrieval of stored artifacts requires careful handling."

commands.name: bank
commands.summary: List what is in your bank deposit box
details_html: Every character has a deposit box at Arkham Savings & Trust that only they can open. Items you
leave behind when you exit the tutorial end up here.
• bank - List the contents of your deposit box
• You must be in a bank to use bank, deposit and withdraw
• The box holds 100 stacks; a full box refuses deposits until you withdraw something

commands.name: deposit
commands.summary: Deposit an item from your inventory into your bank deposit box
details_html: Store an item from your inventory in your deposit box. Only you can open it.
• You can use item names or inventory numbers
• You can specify quantity to deposit only part of a stack

commands.name: withdraw
commands.summary: Withdraw an item from your bank deposit box into your inventory
details_html: Take an item out of your deposit box and into your inventory.
• You can use item names or the numbers shown by bank

commands.name: go
commands.summary: Move in a specific direction
details_html: Traverse the non-Euclidean corridors of our world. Each step brings you closer to revelations best left undiscovered.
You must be on your feet to move, and you cannot walk away from a fight (use flee). Moving breaks off any rest in progress.
Remember: "The geometry of this place is not as it seems." - Prof. Armitage

commands.name: say
commands.summary: Speak to other players in your current room

examples.input: say What a strange place this is...

details_html: Project your voice into the eldritch air, allowing your words to reach
the ears of those who share your current location. As the ancient texts
suggest, communication is the first step toward understanding.
• say [message] - Speak to players in your current room
Note: Your words will be heard by all players currently in the same room.

commands.name: talk
commands.summary: Speak with an NPC through a dialogue tree (private to you)
details_html: Begin or continue a private conversation with an NPC who has a dialogue tree.
Replies appear as personal system messages (not room chat). Leaving the room
• talk <npc> - Start (or restart) dialogue with an NPC in your room
• talk <number> - Choose a numbered reply from the current options
• The NPC must be in the same room
• Not every NPC has a dialogue tree; those without will say they have nothing to say
• Choose an option whose next is empty (or farewell) to end the conversation
• Quest ask/turnin remain separate: use quest ask / quest turnin
As noted in the restricted stacks: conversation is a lantern in the dark.

commands.name: me
commands.summary: Describe an action in the third person; the line is shown to you.
details_html: Your name is placed in front of the action, so me studies the map reads as your character studying the map.
At present the line is shown only to you. To have everyone in the room see it, use emote.

commands.name: pose
commands.summary: Set your character's pose or description

examples.input: pose is reading an ancient tome

details_html: Set a persistent description of what your character is doing or how they appear. Others see it when they look at you or at the room.
It stays until you change it. Use pose with no description to clear it.

commands.name: alias
commands.summary: Create or view command aliases
details_html: Create shortcuts for commonly used commands. Aliases allow you to define
your own command names for frequently used actions.
• Alias names must start with a letter
After creating an alias, you can use the alias name as a command.

commands.name: aliases
commands.summary: List all your aliases
details_html: View all the aliases you have created for quick command access.
This will show you all your current aliases and what commands they execute.

commands.name: unalias
commands.summary: Remove a command alias
details_html: Remove an alias that you no longer need or want to change.
After removing an alias, you can create a new one with the same name if desired.

commands.name: help
commands.summary: Get help on commands
details_html: Access the ancient knowledge contained within these digital scrolls.
Learn about available commands and their proper usage.
• help - Show general help and command categories
• help [command] - Get detailed help for a specific command
Use this command whenever you need guidance on how to use the game's features.

commands.name: npc
commands.summary: NPC management commands (admin only)

examples.input: npc create TestNPC shopkeeper arkhamcity_downtown earth_arkhamcity_downtown_001

details_html: As documented in the Cultes des Goules, proper administrative protocols
are essential for maintaining control over the eldritch entities that
lurk in the shadows of our world.
• npc create <name> <type> <sub_zone_id> <room_id> - Create a new NPC definition
Note: These commands require admin privileges. Only administrators
can manage NPCs in the world.

commands.name: who
commands.summary: List online players with their levels and locations
details_html: Peer into the shadows to see which fellow investigators are currently active
in our realm. This command reveals the presence of other players, their levels,
• who - List all online players with levels and locations
• who [name] - Search for specific players by name (case-insensitive partial matching)
Online Players (3): alice [5] - Arkham: City: Northside Intersection Derby Garrison,
bob [3] - Arkham: City: Northside Room Derby St 001,
charlie [7] [ADMIN] - Arkham: City: Northside Room High Ln 002
Players matching 'al' (1): alice [5] - Arkham: City: Northside Intersection Derby Garrison
No players found matching 'xyz'. Try 'who' to see all online players.
As the ancient texts suggest: "Knowledge of one's companions is the first step toward survival in the face of the unknown."

commands.name: catalog
commands.summary: Browse the item prototype catalog (paginated text table)
details_html: List item prototypes from the archives. Prints a short paginated table in-game.
Players see name, type, and short description; administrators see full prototype
fields. For the rich HTML table, open ESC Main Menu and choose Catalog.
• catalog - First page of all prototypes (sorted by name)
• catalog search=<q> - Search name, description, or id
• Bare words without key=value are treated as search text

commands.name: cast
commands.summary: Cast a learned spell
details_html: Harness the eldritch forces that lie beyond the veil of reality. Casting spells requires
Magic Points (MP) and, for Mythos spells, lucidity. The forbidden knowledge exacts its price.
• cast [spell_name] - Cast a spell on yourself (self-target spells)
• cast [spell_name] [target] - Cast a spell on a specific target
• You must have learned the spell first (use /learn, /teach, or /read)
• Some spells require material components (consumed on cast)
• Spells with casting times require you to wait - use /stop to interrupt
• In combat, if no target is specified, the spell targets your combat opponent
• Casting spells with casting times waits for your turn in combat
• You can interrupt casting with /stop (may cost MP if LUCK check fails)
Your mastery level affects spell effectiveness and success chance. Mastery increases
with successful casts. Use /spells to see your learned spells and mastery levels.
Warning: "That which calls upon the void may yet call back." - Prof. Armitage

commands.name: spells
commands.summary: List all learned spells with mastery levels
details_html: Review your accumulated arcane knowledge. This command displays all spells you have
learned along with your current mastery level for each.
• spells - List all your learned spells with mastery percentages
• Spell Name - Mastery: XX% - Each learned spell with mastery level
• Higher mastery improves spell effectiveness and success chance
Learn new spells using /learn, or be taught by an NPC with /teach.
Some spells can be learned from spellbooks using /read.
As the Necronomicon warns: "Knowledge gained is knowledge that cannot be unlearned."

commands.name: spell
commands.summary: Show detailed information about a specific spell
details_html: Examine the intricate details of a specific spell. This command reveals the spell's
costs, effects, requirements, and your current mastery level if you know it.
• spell [spell_name] - Show detailed information about a spell
• MP Cost - Magic Points required to cast
• Corruption on Cast - Corruption gained (some Mythos spells)
• Casting Time - Time in seconds before spell completes
• Target Type - Who/what the spell can target
• Range - How far the spell can reach
• Your Mastery - Your mastery level (if learned) or "Not learned"
• You can view spell information even if you haven't learned it
• Use this to plan which spells to learn
• Material components marked as "(consumed)" are used up when casting
• Material components marked as "(reusable)" are not consumed
Remember: "Understanding the cost of power is the first lesson in wielding it."

commands.name: learn
commands.summary: Learn a spell by name.
details_html: Acquire new arcane knowledge by naming the spell you wish to learn. This is a stopgap while quests and vendors are not yet able to teach spells.
Spells can also be had from a spellbook with read, or from an NPC teacher with teach.
Once learned, use spells to see your repertoire and spell to study one in detail.
Warning: "The price of forbidden knowledge is often paid in sanity." - Cultes des Goules

commands.name: teach
commands.summary: Learn a spell from an NPC teacher in your room.
details_html: Some who dwell in this world know spells and will share them. Find such a teacher, stand in the same room, and ask for the spell by name.
The teacher must be an NPC; you cannot learn this way from another player.
Forbidden knowledge can leave its mark. If the spell taints the mind, you are told so when the lesson ends.

arguments.name: npc_name
arguments.description: The teacher: an NPC in your room.

arguments.name: spell_name
arguments.description: The spell you wish to be taught.

commands.name: stop
commands.summary: Interrupt your current spell casting
details_html: Abandon your current spell casting attempt. Interrupting a spell mid-cast is dangerous
and may cost you Magic Points depending on your luck.
• You're casting a spell with a casting time and want to cancel it
• You need to change tactics during combat
• You realize you're casting the wrong spell
• A LUCK check determines if you avoid MP loss
• If LUCK check passes: No MP lost, casting stops safely
• If LUCK check fails: You lose the spell's MP cost
• Spell does not complete and has no effect
• Only works if you are currently casting a spell
• Instant cast spells (0 casting time) cannot be interrupted
• Material components already consumed are not refunded
• Useful for canceling long casting times when needed
Warning: "Interrupting the flow of eldritch power is not without risk."

commands.name: local
commands.summary: Speak to everyone in your current sub-zone.

arguments.name: message
arguments.description: What you say. Long messages are rejected.

examples.input: local Has anyone seen the librarian?

commands.name: global
commands.summary: Speak to every investigator on the server. Gated by character level.

arguments.name: message
arguments.description: What you say to the whole server.

examples.input: global Does anyone know a way into the Miskatonic stacks?

details_html: If your character is not yet experienced enough, the server tells you so instead of sending the message.

commands.name: whisper
commands.summary: Send a private message to one player.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: The player to address.

arguments.name: message
arguments.description: What you whisper.

examples.input: whisper Armitage The seal is cracked.

commands.name: reply
commands.summary: Answer the last player who whispered to you.

arguments.name: message
arguments.description: Your answer.

examples.input: reply I will meet you at the library.

commands.name: emote
commands.summary: Perform an action that everyone in the room sees.

arguments.name: action
arguments.description: The action to perform.

commands.name: channel
commands.summary: Switch to a chat channel, or set your default channel.

arguments.name: channel_name
arguments.description: The channel to use.

commands.name: mute
commands.summary: Silence a player for yourself, optionally for a limited time.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: The player to mute.

arguments.name: duration_in_minutes
arguments.description: How long the mute lasts, up to one week. Omit for a permanent mute.

details_html: A mute is personal: it applies to you alone.

commands.name: unmute
commands.summary: Lift a mute you placed on a player.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: The player to unmute.

commands.name: mutes
commands.summary: Show every mute currently in effect for you, with expiry times.

commands.name: follow
commands.summary: Follow a player or NPC in your room as they move.

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: A player or NPC in the same room.

details_html: Following an NPC takes effect at once. Following a player needs their consent: they are sent a request, which lapses if they do not answer.
You can follow only one target at a time. If you cannot make the same move as them, or cannot get to your feet, you lose them.

commands.name: unfollow
commands.summary: Stop following whoever you are following.

commands.name: following
commands.summary: Show who you are following and who is following you.

commands.name: party
commands.summary: Form and manage an adventuring party.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: Required for invite and kick: the player's name.

details_html: With no subcommand, party shows your party's status.

Only the leader may invite, kick, or disband. An invited player is asked to accept or decline, and the invitation lapses if they do not answer. A player can belong to only one party, and the invited player must be in the same room.
Parties are not remembered: if the leader leaves or disconnects, the party is dissolved.

commands.name: journal
commands.summary: Read your quest log.

commands.name: quest
commands.summary: Ask an NPC about a quest, turn one in, or abandon one.

arguments.name: npc
arguments.description: For ask and turnin: the NPC to speak with.

arguments.name: quest name
arguments.description: For abandon: the quest's common name.

commands.name: status
commands.summary: Show your character's current condition.

commands.name: whoami
commands.summary: Show your own status. Works exactly like status.

commands.name: skills
commands.summary: List your character's skills.

commands.name: time
commands.summary: Show the current Mythos time and any holidays in effect.

commands.name: quit
commands.summary: Leave the game.

commands.name: logout
commands.summary: Log out cleanly: your session is closed and your connections dropped.

commands.name: rest
commands.summary: Withdraw from the world and disconnect cleanly.
details_html: In an inn, hotel, or motel, resting disconnects you at once. Anywhere else you sit down and a short countdown begins.
Combat, moving, or casting a spell breaks the countdown. Chatting, looking, and handling your inventory do not. You cannot rest while in combat.

commands.name: inventory
commands.summary: List what you carry and wear, including the contents of containers.

commands.name: pickup
commands.summary: Pick up an item lying in the room.

arguments.name: item
arguments.description: The item's number in the room list, or part of its name.

arguments.name: quantity
arguments.description: How many to take. Defaults to the whole stack.

commands.name: drop
commands.summary: Drop an item from your inventory into the room.

arguments.name: inventory-number
arguments.description: The item's slot number in your inventory.

arguments.name: quantity
arguments.description: How many to drop. Defaults to the whole stack.

examples.note: Drop five of the items in slot 2.

commands.name: equip
commands.summary: Wield or wear an item from your inventory.

arguments.name: item
arguments.description: The item's slot number, or part of its name.

arguments.name: slot
arguments.description: Which slot to put it in, when it could go in more than one.

commands.name: unequip
commands.summary: Take off or put away something you have equipped.

arguments.name: slot
arguments.description: The slot to empty, or the equipped item's name.

commands.name: use
commands.summary: Use a consumable from your inventory.

arguments.name: item
arguments.description: The item's slot number, or part of its name.

commands.name: read
commands.summary: Read a spellbook to learn a spell from it.

arguments.name: item_name
arguments.description: The book to read.

arguments.name: spell_name
arguments.description: Which spell to learn, when the book holds several. Optional if it holds only one.

commands.name: sit
commands.summary: Sit down.

commands.name: stand
commands.summary: Return to your feet.

commands.name: lie
commands.summary: Lie down on the ground.

commands.name: attack
commands.summary: Attack a creature in your room.

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: The creature's name. Only NPCs can be attacked.

details_html: You cannot attack while incapacitated, or while protective wards still shield you.

commands.name: punch
commands.summary: Another way to attack: works exactly like attack.

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: The creature's name.

commands.name: kick
commands.summary: Another way to attack: works exactly like attack.

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: The creature's name.

commands.name: strike
commands.summary: Another way to attack: works exactly like attack.

arguments.name: target
arguments.description: The creature's name.

commands.name: flee
commands.summary: Break away from combat into a random adjacent room.
details_html: You must be in combat. A failed attempt costs your round and draws free blows. If you are not on your feet, getting up uses the attempt and you must try again.

commands.name: taunt
commands.summary: Spend your round drawing a creature's attention onto you.

arguments.name: npc
arguments.description: A creature already fighting in your room.

details_html: The roll is Intimidate or Fighting, whichever is higher. A strong roll holds the creature firmly, a failure does nothing, and a fumble makes it ignore you.
You must already be fighting the creature, in the same room. Only NPCs can be taunted.

commands.name: assist
commands.summary: Join the fight a player is in and attack their foe.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: Whose fight to join. With no name, you join your party leader's fight.

details_html: Once you join, you fight on your own until the fight ends.

commands.name: protect
commands.summary: Spend your round covering an ally so blows aimed at them land on you.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: An ally in your room.

details_html: The roll is Fighting. On a success, blows aimed at your ally land on you for the rest of this round and the next; a strong roll adds a round. You also hold more of the creature's attention, and part of your ally's share of it passes to you. A miss does nothing. You can join their fight this way.

commands.name: cleanse
commands.summary: Perform a cleansing rite that pares back the corruption clinging to you.
details_html: The rite cannot be repeated at once. If you try too soon, you are told how long to wait.

commands.name: ground
commands.summary: Begin a ritual to bring a catatonic ally back to their senses.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: An ally whose mind has shattered, within reach.

details_html: The ritual takes time to work. Moving, casting a spell, entering combat, or a disconnect by either of you interrupts it. You cannot begin it during combat, and the target must actually be catatonic.

commands.name: system
commands.summary: Broadcast a system message to every player.

arguments.name: message
arguments.description: The announcement.

commands.name: mute_global
commands.summary: Silence a player for everyone, optionally for a limited time.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: The player to silence.

arguments.name: duration_in_minutes
arguments.description: How long, up to one week. Omit for permanent.

arguments.name: reason
arguments.description: Why, for the record.

commands.name: unmute_global
commands.summary: Lift a global mute.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: The player to restore.

commands.name: add_admin
commands.summary: Grant administrator privileges to a player.

arguments.name: player
arguments.description: The player to promote.

commands.name: admin
commands.summary: Administrative utilities, chosen by subcommand.

arguments.name: subcommand
arguments.description: status, time, set, or setlucidity (also written lcd).

commands.name: summon
commands.summary: Conjure an item or NPC into your current room.

arguments.name: prototype_id
arguments.description: The prototype to conjure.

arguments.name: quantity
arguments.description: How many, from 1 to 5. Defaults to 1.

arguments.name: item|npc
arguments.description: What kind of prototype it is. Defaults to item.

commands.name: teleport
commands.summary: Bring a player to your location, or to a room beside it.

arguments.name: player_name
arguments.description: The player to move.

arguments.name: direction
arguments.description: Send them to the adjoining room in this direction instead.

commands.name: goto
commands.summary: Go to a player's location.

arguments.name: player_name
arguments.description: The player to join.

commands.name: shutdown
commands.summary: Shut the server down after a countdown, or cancel one in progress.

arguments.name: seconds
arguments.description: Countdown length. Defaults to a short countdown if omitted.
